svg.text: Stage 1 · Turning the 4×4 Board into a Fast Cheat Sheet
Done once per board: load all 16 letters together, number them A=0..Z=25, and give each tile a shelf & switch.
A. Load all 16 squares at once & turn letters into numbers (0..25)

g.text: All 16 tiles sit side-by-side inside one 128-bit CPU register (lane 0..15):
Uppercase all 16 at once & turn A..Z → 0..25 (invalid '?' → 26✕)
Any invalid character (not A–Z) clamps safely to 26 so it can never match a dictionary letter.

svg.text: B. Why split each number? The alphabet lives on "4 Shelves of 8 Switches"
Later (Stage 3), each dictionary node stores its valid next letters as 26 on/off switches grouped into 4 bytes (shelves). Pre-label every tile now!

g.text: Example: How tile @2 'T' (19) finds its slot

svg.text: All 16 tiles are prepped in a handful of vector ops once — then reused hundreds of times during the search.
